content.text:
The day view is now cached in Redis. The cache is in the new `src/lib/scheduleCache.ts` and is wired into `schedule/today/route.ts`. The key is `clinic:schedule:today:<practitionerId>` with a 60-second expiry, so it holds no patient id and one practitioner's day can't be served to another. The cached value is the endpoint's response unchanged (ids, times, status, patient names), so the format is the same and it contains no visit reasons or notes. The existing tests and typecheck pass (`npm run verify`), but I didn't add a test for the cache or the revoke behaviour.

`POST /api/admin/care-team/revoke` now deletes that practitioner's cache entry, so the patient is gone on the next call. Booking an appointment deletes it too, so new bookings show up straight away. A Redis failure on read or write falls back to MySQL, but a failed delete on revoke raises an error instead of being swallowed.

The cached response includes patient names, which are PHI but not clinical content. If you'd rather keep names out of Redis, the cache would need to store ids only and look the names up in MySQL on each call, which defeats part of the point of caching.
